name: NutriRoute Cart Vendor All-Weather Stand Kit
description: A street food vendor's full working kit, built for twelve-hour outdoor shifts in M88's acid-tinged weather and the crushing foot traffic of Circuit-level plazas. The foundation is a long-sleeved fitted base layer in white moisture-wicking synth-cotton, worn under a NutriRoute-branded bib apron in bright saffron yellow with wide chest straps and a front kangaroo pocket large enough to hold a payment terminal, two seasoning pouches, and a folded rain hood. The apron's fabric has a food-safe antimicrobial coating and a water-resistant outer face. Over the base layer, a charcoal zip-through hoodie provides warmth during low-traffic hours; the hood is lined in the same saffron yellow as the apron, visible when thrown back. Wide-leg black cargo trousers in a light synth-canvas have a deep rear pocket on each leg and a knee patch in the same saffron yellow — a NutriRoute brand consistency requirement that vendors quietly resent. Footwear is a pair of black slip-resistant clogs with a closed toe, waterproof upper, and a cushioned insole rated for all-day standing on hard surface. A flat-brimmed saffron cap with a NutriRoute logo embroidered in white sits on the crown, often worn slightly tilted. The kit reads loud and cheerful in color, worn and personal in texture.
materials: saffron synth-canvas bib apron (antimicrobial, water-resistant coating)
charcoal zip-through hoodie with saffron hood lining
functionality: Food-safe antimicrobial apron coating, large kangaroo apron pocket for payment terminal and supplies, water-resistant outer fabric for acid rain exposure, slip-resistant all-day standing footwear, integrated rain hood in kangaroo pocket, layered temperature regulation for outdoor all-weather shifts.
what_it_says: You know your regulars by order, not name. You've been at the same corner for six years and you know who's late for work and who's been crying and who's carrying something they shouldn't be. The saffron is loud and you've learned to use that — nobody looks twice at the cart vendor. You see everything. You remember everything.
manufacturer: NutriRoute (corponation-branded vendor uniform program; apron and cap issued, remaining pieces vendor-sourced within brand color compliance guidelines)
price_range: Φ140–Φ210 (apron and cap company-issued; remaining pieces self-purchased within spec)
story_hooks: A NutriRoute vendor at a specific Circuit plaza has been quietly keeping a handwritten log of everyone who passes their cart between 0600 and 0900 — they've noticed a pattern in the foot traffic that suggests a synchronized movement of people that has nothing to do with commuting.

The large kangaroo pocket of a vendor's apron has been used as a dead-drop for months — small packages, folded notes, once a very small firearm — and the vendor wants out of the arrangement but doesn't know how to safely refuse.

The saffron uniform makes the vendor instantly recognizable across the plaza, which is exactly why someone is impersonating them — a fake NutriRoute cart has appeared two blocks east, staffed by someone who doesn't quite know the menu.

physical_description.visual_profile: A street vendor's practical uniform kit that projects accessible service-industry friendliness through high-visibility saffron accents against neutral base layers. The silhouette is functional and approachable — fitted enough to move freely during long shifts, loose enough to layer and adjust. The bright yellow apron dominates the visual center, grounding the outfit in NutriRoute brand identity. Overall impression: cheerful but worn, corporate-issued but personalized through twelve-hour shifts.
physical_description.fit: Fitted white base layer hugs the torso for moisture management; charcoal hoodie worn open or layered with a relaxed, unstudied fit; cargo trousers cut wide through the leg for stability and deep-pocket functionality; closed-toe clogs with secure slip-resistant soles accommodate eight-to-twelve hour standing shifts without arch collapse.
physical_description.primary_material: White moisture-wicking synth-cotton base layer; saffron polyester-blend bib apron with antimicrobial food-safe coating and water-resistant outer face; charcoal heather cotton-synth blend hoodie; light synth-canvas black cargo trousers; black waterproof slip-resistant clogs with cushioned EVA insoles.
physical_description.texture: Base layer smooth and slightly elastic against skin; apron fabric has a subtle sheen from antimicrobial treatment, crisp yet broken-in at stress points (straps, pocket edges); hoodie soft and slightly pilled from repeated washing; cargo trousers have a utilitarian weave with slight surface texture; clogs feature a grippy treaded sole worn smooth in high-contact areas.
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary: bright saffron yellow (apron, hoodie lining, cap, knee patch) — NutriRoute brand-mandated; secondary: charcoal gray (hoodie), black (cargo trousers, clogs); accent: white (base layer, cap embroidery, apron straps). High contrast and intentionally visible for food-service safety and brand recognition.
physical_description.closures: White base layer has a crew neck; charcoal hoodie has a full-length brass zipper, slightly tarnished from daily use; saffron apron fastens via two wide shoulder straps that buckle or hook to a rear waistband; cargo trousers secured with a standard brass zipper fly and snap waistband; clogs are slip-on with no closures.
distinctive_features: NutriRoute-embroidered logo on saffron cap and apron chest
Antimicrobial coating on apron visible as slight sheen under fluorescent lighting
Kangaroo pocket on apron large enough to hold payment terminal and two seasoning pouches
Saffron-yellow lined hood on charcoal hoodie — a functional brand requirement
Knee patches in saffron on black cargo trousers — mandated by vendor guidelines, often resented
Deep rear leg pockets on cargo trousers for small tools or personal items
Cushioned slip-resistant clogs with closed waterproof toe — rated for sixteen-hour continuous standing
Flat-brimmed saffron cap slightly tilted, showing wear at visor edge
Visible creasing and minor stains on apron at pocket edge and lower hem — evidence of heavy use
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 functional/working class. NutriRoute is a mid-tier corponation vendor network serving Circuit-level plazas in the GLMZ. The kit is standardized, company-issued, and practical — not luxury, but reliable. Color-coding and uniform requirements signal corporate oversight without the polish of Tier 1-2 corporate dress.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street-level service worker in the gig economy tier of the GLMZ. Wearing this outfit immediately identifies the wearer as a NutriRoute franchise vendor — visible, tracked, and part of a corporate-managed network. The outfit says: 'I am accessible, I am fed-regulated, I am part of the machine.' Sub-grade workers and street vendors may view it with ambivalence — a step up from salvage-tier but still bound to corporate color codes and shift schedules.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and worn. The apron shows faint stains at the pocket and hem from daily food handling (turmeric, oil, acidic condiments). The hoodie has minor pilling and a slightly faded appearance from repeated industrial laundering. Cargo trousers show creasing at the knees and minor fraying at the inner leg seams. Clogs have a scuffed appearance on the outer heel and sole tread worn smooth in high-impact zones. The cap brim shows sweat stains on the underside and the embroidery is slightly loose at the edge. Nothing broken — everything functional.
